thread:
sahil: Hey infra — prepping production onboarding for 3 new customer projects. Need quota + project approval for GPUs and egress IPs. TL;DR: us-central1: +40 A100 (v4), +120 L4, +8 H100; europe-west4: +16 A100, +40 L4. Also Cloud NAT ephemeral external IP limit and reserved EIP quota might block us. Can we get a preflight and greenlight to open requests?

maria: Which projects are these and what's steady-state vs burst? we need a quick cost estimate before I sign off on billing anchors.

sahil: Projects: redwood-prod-custA, redwood-prod-custB, redwood-prod-pilot. Steady: ~60% of requested capacity, with short hourly bursts for custA. Estimated GPU hours ~120k GPUh/mo across all projects. Rough cost ballpark $180k/mo for GPUs+egress.

aj: For quota strategy I'd prefer shared VPC with centralized NAT + pooled GPU quota behind Dedicated. Avoid per-project EIP requests by using Cloud NAT with multiple external IPs. We still need static IPs for LBs and external webhook endpoints.

irene: Security flagged custB as private-only (no public IP). That changes NAT requirements — we'll need internal-only H100 nodes and VPC peering.

luca: Filing quota tickets now. Also need billing contact and org node for each project. @maria can you confirm contacts?

devops-bot: Ticket created: Q-2026-438 for A100 quota in us-central1. Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/Q-2026-438

maria: Billing contacts added to the onboarding sheet: ops+billing@redwood.ai, finance@redwood.ai. I added a cost calc tab with conservative and aggressive scenarios.

sahil: We're hitting org-level static external IP limit (default 80). Proposal: reserve 100 static IPs in us-central1, 50 in europe-west4. If GCP resists, fallback to Cloud NAT with regional prefix pooling.

aj: Can you paste outputs for `gcloud compute addresses list --filter='status=RESERVED'` and `gcloud compute regions describe us-central1 --project=redwood-prod-infra`? Need to know per-project vs org quota remaining.

sahil: Pasted a short excerpt to #eng-infra-files (link). Quick cut:
```
RESERVED addrs: us-central1: 12 reserved, project limit 24
europe-west4: 6 reserved, project limit 15
ORG static ip quota remaining: 14
```

irene: For private deployment we should request H100 quota in a separate VPC with no external IPs. Can we reserve H100 nodes behind an internal load balancer? Ops: @aj?

aj: Yes. In the quota request include 'no external IPs' and mention internal LB for inference endpoints. Use exact acceleratorType string and include expected sustained CPU/ram and GPU utilization. Support usually asks for that.

luca: Created Q-2026-439 for europe-west4 increases and attached network diagram. Estimated incremental cost in ticket: $150k/mo. Looping in sales for enterprise commit.

devops-bot: Quota request submitted to Google Cloud: requestId=RQ-99211. Expected reply 3-5 business days.

maria: One more ask — can we approve using preemptible A100 for noncritical batch jobs? saves ~70% cost. Any objections?

sahil: OK for batch. For low-latency inference lanes we require on-demand A100/H100.

aj: Plan a canary for custA using reserved capacity, fallback to L4 variants for degraded performance. Also add auto-fallback routing in the serving layer.

irene: I can approve security exceptions for the pilot if we get E2E encryption + KMS integration documented. I'll sign once docs are uploaded.

sahil: I'll assemble artifacts: spreadsheet, org/project nodes, IAM matrix, network design, and post links here.

luca: Updated ticket: attached `gcloud compute regions describe` output and network diagram. Will follow up with support contact details when available.

devops-bot: Support replied: need org admin approval for quotas >50 A100. Please escalate to @marcus-admin.

marcus-admin: Escalating to finance/legal for commit approval. @maria please forward the cost breakdown and expected 12mo run rate.

maria: Forwarded — finance queued for Monday review.

sahil: Pinging to keep this on radar. If we don't get quota in 7 days we'll schedule partial routing to europe-west4 and adjust the routing policies (latency/cost).
